title: FounderGate Cage Evidence Ledger Event
description: SCAFFOLD ONLY. An append-only cage-evidence event. A cage is an OUTER-CAGE trust boundary that DENIES egress, HOLDS actions, and serves MOCK responses instead of any live provider crossing. HARD DOCTRINE encoded here: caged/held is NOT live proof. This schema deliberately has NO live/provider source type and NO verdict value that asserts a live crossing. Every event MUST carry a SOURCE (a sourceless event is not evidence and is rejected). Final cage claims require independent Checker + Advisor verification and are NOT self-certified by this record.

id.description: Stable, unique id for this event within a ledger.

ts.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the cage-evidence event was recorded.

kind.description: The class of cage-evidence this event records.

cage_id.description: Identifier of the cage instance that produced this evidence.

policy_hash.description: Hex digest of the cage policy under which this evidence was produced. A hash, never a secret or the policy body.

denied_egress.description: Egress attempts the cage DENIED (never allowed out). Present chiefly on egress_denied events.

held_actions.description: Actions the cage HELD (not fired). Held is not fired; held is not live.

mock_responses.description: Mock responses served in place of any live call. A mock is UNVERIFIED by construction — it proves cage wiring, never a real-world outcome.

tests.description: Test outcomes attached to this evidence event.

checker_verdict.description: Independent Checker verdict. null = not yet verified. No value asserts a live crossing.

advisor_verdict.description: Independent Advisor verdict. null = not yet reviewed. No value asserts a live crossing.

founder_decision.description: Founder decision on the caged evidence. PENDING/null = no decision. APPROVE here approves the CAGED record only — it never authorizes a live crossing on its own.

note.description: Optional one-line human context. No secrets, no PII.

seq.description: Zero-based position in the append-only chain. Set by the writer.

prev_chain_hash.description: Chain hash of the prior event, or null for the first event. Set by the writer.

chain_hash.description: sha256(prev_chain_hash + canonical(event-without-chain-fields)). Set by the writer; makes the ledger tamper-evident.

source.description: Provenance of the event. HARD RULE: no cage-evidence event is evidence without one of these source types AND a non-empty ref. There is deliberately NO live/provider source type — cage evidence can never grade as live. Grades: cage_log/command_output/local_file are VERIFIABLE (a third party can re-check the artifact); checker/advisor/founder are ASSERTED (an independent party's word, traceable but not machine-verifiable); mock/planned are UNVERIFIED (labels a simulated or intended event honestly).

ref.description: Pointer to the source: a cage log line/id, the exact command run, a repo-relative file path, a checker/advisor verdict id, a founder note author, or a mock/plan marker. Must be non-empty so the claim can be traced.

detail.description: Optional extra provenance detail (exit code, line range, verdict id, reviewer login).

target.description: Opaque destination label the cage denied (host tag / channel tag). Never a secret or full credential.

protocol.description: Optional transport tag (e.g. http, dns, smtp).

reason.description: Why the cage denied this egress.

action_class.description: Class of the held action (e.g. send, delete, rsvp, payment). Class only — never a payload.

target_tag.description: Optional opaque target tag. Never a real identifier, address, or PII.

reason.description: Why the action was held rather than fired.

for_action_class.description: Action class the mock stood in for.

shape.description: Human tag describing the mock response shape (e.g. 'ok-stub', 'error-429'). Never a real provider payload.

content_hash.description: Optional hex digest of the mock body. A hash, never the body.
